page: Microsoft Azure EC64ads_cc_v5 is a memory-optimized server instance powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor. Operating on the x86_64 architecture under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, this instance features 64 dedicated virtual CPUs mapped to 32 physical cores with 2 threads per core. The CPU runs at a clock speed of 3.525 GHz and includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. It is equipped with 512.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU, alongside a bundled 2458 GB local disk with Premium Storage capability.

In benchmark evaluations, the server demonstrates strong multi-core and memory subsystem performance. The Passmark memory score ranks in the top tier (top 10%), supported by a strong read-only small-block memory bandwidth of 4162.65 GB/sec. Multi-core processing capabilities are highlighted by strong results in stress-ng multi-core tests, Geekbench multi-core scores, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. However, large-block uncached memory read and write speeds fall into the average category, and single-core performance metrics, such as Geekbench single-core and single-threaded gzip compression, remain within the average range.

The hardware profile offers high resource density, making it a qualitatively cost-efficient choice for memory-intensive workloads that do not require dedicated GPU acceleration. The instance excels in database operations, as evidenced by strong Passmark database and Redis SET operation benchmarks. It is highly suitable for large-scale relational databases, in-memory caching layers, data analytics, and memory-bound enterprise applications. Conversely, the lack of a GPU and weak performance in large-model LLM text generation make it less suitable for heavy deep learning training or complex AI inference tasks.
